title: Clinical Field Specialist
description:
Clinical Field Specialist (CFS) – Women’s Health

Territory: West Texas (Covering Lubbock, Midland, Odessa, Amarillo, Abilene, San Angelo, and El Paso)

Position Summary The Clinical Field Specialist (CFS) will drive revenue growth and market expansion across the West Texas territory through direct engagement with individual Maternal-Fetal Medicine specialists (MFMs), OB/GYNs, and Genetic Counselors. This role focuses on building and maintaining strong clinical relationships while developing and executing strategic business plans that accelerate adoption. The CFS will support both established and newly launched diagnostic products, providing clinical expertise, educational support, and hands-on training in technical product applications.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Revenue & Market Growth: Increase revenue and drive market development through direct consultative sales to individual MFMs, OB/GYNs, and Genetic Counselors across the West Texas region.
  • Relationship Management: Execute effective prospecting strategies while cultivating and maintaining long-term relationships with key clinical stakeholders and decision-makers.
  • Strategic Territory Execution: Create and implement a comprehensive business plan to rapidly grow market share and revenue across a geographically expansive territory.
  • Product Launch & Support: Champion both currently marketed diagnostic assays and new product launches, serving as a clinical and technical resource for accounts.
  • Organizational Impact: Play a critical role in regional and national commercial success by sharing market insights and collaborating cross-functionally.
  • Compliance & Data Security: Work regularly with Protected Health Information (PHI) in both paper and electronic formats, utilizing secure technologies to perform daily job functions.
  • Training Requirements: Complete mandatory training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance, and security within the first 30 days of hire, and maintain current status on all ongoing Natera training requirements.

Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree required; preferred fields include Science, Nursing (RN/NP), or a related healthcare discipline.
  • Experience & Clinical Background: Three (3) years of physician sales experience in the diagnostic laboratory or women's health industry is preferred, though not strictly required for candidates with strong clinical credentials. We are actively open to Nurse Practitioners (NPs) currently working within an MFM or OB/GYN practice looking to transition into a commercial clinical specialist role.
  • Local Ties: Must reside within the West Texas territory; candidates with established roots, local familiarity, and existing clinical relationships in the region are strongly preferred.
  • Market Knowledge: Deep understanding of the OB/GYN and MFM workflow and clinical landscape, with a proven ability to build trust with providers.
  • Launch & Growth Mindset: Demonstrated ability to drive adoption, educate clinical teams, and grow volume in developing or expansive markets.
  • Technical Proficiency: Proficient with Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel, Gmail, and Salesforce.com.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Communication: Strong organizational and presentation skills with the proven ability to communicate complex clinical data effectively to diverse audiences.
  • Territory & Time Management: Exceptional time management and travel-planning skills with the ability to assess, route, and prioritize opportunities effectively across a wide geographic footprint.
  • Strategic Mindset: Adaptable, self-motivated, and results-driven, combining strong interpersonal and analytical skills with the ability to think strategically while executing tactically.
  • Closing Focus: Demonstrates a sense of urgency and a strong focus on closing business and driving consistent test volume.
  • Consultative Problem-Solving: Assesses the operational and clinical needs of medical professionals through consultative sales, logistical coordination, and proactive problem-solving.
  • Collaboration: Works effectively both independently in the field and collaboratively with internal commercial, medical affairs, and customer support teams.

Compensation & Benefits The total on-target earnings (OTE) package includes a competitive base salary along with uncapped quarterly commissions. Beyond OTE, the comprehensive compensation package also features a monthly car allowance, Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), and full corporate benefits.



The compensation package listed is for 1st year OTE, which are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. On-target earnings (OTE) represent the total potential income an employee can earn by achieving 100% of their performance goals. It combines a base salary with commissions and serves as an estimated figure rather than a guaranteed amount, providing a guideline based on average performance outcomes.

On-target earnings (OTE)
$165,000—$195,000 USD

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program!

title: Order Resolution Program Manager
description:
Positition:

The Order Resolution Program Manager builds and leads the Order Resolution Program (ORP), a national program that helps ensure patients receive the testing their physicians have ordered. When an order encounters a barrier, such as an unreachable patient, an incorrect phone number, a patient with unanswered questions about their test, or a step that requires clinic involvement, this role makes sure the right people take the right action so care is not delayed. Many of these patients are navigating a cancer diagnosis, and the program exists to support them and the Patient Coordinators who care for them.

As the program's founding owner, the Program Manager exercises independent judgment to assess the current landscape, resolve complex cases directly, and determine what the program needs to succeed, including whether and how to expand the team. The role is hands-on by design: the Program Manager works open cases alongside Patient Coordinators to understand where and why orders stall, then uses that firsthand insight and program data to set strategy, define standards, and guide leadership decisions.

The Program Manager partners across Patient Services, Territory Managers, Clinical Oncology Specialists, Patient Coordinators, Inside Sales Managers, Regional Directors, and Operations Managers, earning alignment through expertise and sound judgment rather than direct authority.

 

Primary Responsibilities:

Program Strategy & Ownership

  • Own the Order Resolution Program end-to-end across all national regions, independently assessing the current landscape, including case volume, root causes, regional variation, and existing workflows, to determine where patient orders are most at risk of delay.
  • Develop a data-supported program roadmap and staffing recommendation for Patient Services leadership, including headcount requirements, staffing structure, timeline, and whether process or tooling solutions would better serve patients.
  • Define the program operating model, including case ownership, escalation criteria, service timelines, handoff protocols, and quality standards, and adjust it as the program matures.
  • Lead the design of the team structure, role definitions, hiring profile, onboarding, and performance expectations for future team members.

Case Resolution & Patient Care Support

  • Exercise independent judgment to evaluate open ORP cases, determine the root cause of each barrier, and develop a tailored resolution strategy that accounts for the clinical context, the patient's circumstances, and available resources.
  • Work complex and high-priority cases directly, including researching LIMS, paper orders, and patient outreach tools to locate missing or updated contact information, and decide whether a case calls for administrative resolution, clinic education or engagement, or escalation.
  • Partner with Patient Coordinators to support patient outreach, providing guidance on how to approach each case and, where appropriate, connecting with patients directly so that questions about their orders are answered and care can move forward.
  • Determine when to escalate a case to the clinic, engage the field team, or close it, and document the rationale so any subsequent owner can continue seamlessly.
  • Maintain a real-time view of all open cases, including status, owner, next action, and age, and follow up consistently to confirm actions are completed and patients are not left waiting.

Analytics & Performance Reporting

  • Design, build, and maintain the ORP reporting infrastructure, including dashboards, KPI scorecards, and regional trend analysis, and define the metrics used to measure program success.
  • Report regularly to Patient Services leadership on case volume, resolution rates, time to resolution, and order completion outcomes, translating data into clear insights about what is working, what is not, and what should change.
  • Analyze recurring barriers, such as common reasons patients cannot be reached or questions that arise repeatedly, and develop recommendations that reduce the number of patients whose orders require intervention in the first place.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Process Improvement

  • Partner with Territory Managers, Clinical Oncology Specialists, Associate Clinical Oncology Specialists, and Patient Coordinators to set clear expectations, communicate promptly, and share accountability on every open case.
  • Partner with Inside Sales Managers, Regional Directors, and Operations Managers to align program priorities, resolve regional barriers, and ensure teams understand their role in supporting patient orders.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert for ORP, providing guidance and consultation to field and operations partners and developing best practices, training, and standard work that can be adopted nationally.
  • Identify systemic process gaps and bring structured, data-backed recommendations to leadership, including changes to workflows, status definitions, tooling, and cross-team handoffs, with the patient experience as the guiding lens.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

 

Qualifications:

 

  • Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, life sciences, or a related field; or equivalent professional experience in a role requiring independent judgment, program ownership, and decision-making in a healthcare or clinical operations environment.
  • 5 or more years of experience in healthcare operations, patient services, program or project management, or a comparable environment, with demonstrated ownership of a program, workflow, or initiative from assessment through execution.
  • Demonstrated ability to assess a complex operating landscape, identify root causes, and develop and present a data-supported recommendation, including resourcing and staffing needs, to senior leadership.
  • Proven ability to independently assess multi-variable situations and determine the appropriate course of action without direct supervision, particularly in patient-facing or clinically sensitive contexts.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and drive accountability across cross-functional teams, including field, sales, and operations leaders, without direct authority.
  • Strong analytical capability, including building performance reporting, interpreting trends, and communicating findings clearly to leadership; advanced MS Excel or equivalent skills required.
  • Experience in a call center, patient outreach, or high-volume case management environment (inbound and outbound).
  • Proficiency in CRM platforms, case tracking systems, and data tools; familiarity with skip tracing tools and LIMS is a strong plus.
  • Prior experience leading, coaching, or building a team is preferred. Background in patient coordination or another patient-facing healthcare role is strongly preferred.

 

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Technical

  • Program and project management expertise, including scoping, planning, prioritization, milestone tracking, and stakeholder management.
  • Specialized knowledge of healthcare operations, patient services workflows, and clinical coordination sufficient to evaluate case scenarios and develop resolution strategies without relying on standardized scripts.
  • Advanced proficiency in CRM platforms, case tracking systems, and reporting tools, with the ability to design KPI dashboards that give leadership real-time visibility into program performance and patient order outcomes.
  • Strong quantitative skills, including comfort working with large data sets to identify trends, build business cases, and model staffing and capacity needs.
  • Experience with skip tracing tools and multi-database research methods, and with process documentation and standard operating procedure development.

Behavioral

  • Exercises sound, independent judgment consistently, treating each case and each program decision as a situation requiring individualized analysis.
  • Builds before being asked: sees what a new program needs, takes ownership of the decision, and moves forward without waiting to be told something is off track.
  • Balances urgency and care: moves quickly because patients are waiting, and makes thoughtful decisions because the stakes are real.
  • Thinks like a program owner and acts like a teammate: comfortable working individual cases to learn the work, and equally comfortable stepping back to set strategy and advise leadership.
  • Earns credibility with cross-functional partners through expertise, clear communication, and follow-through, and uses it to drive action across teams they do not directly control.
  • Coaches and develops others, and is ready to build and lead a team as the program grows.

 

Physical Demands & Work Environment:

  • This is a primarily remote position. Occasional on-site attendance may be required for planning sessions, leadership reviews, or business needs.
  • Duties are performed in a home office or professional office setting and require the ability to use a computer keyboard, communicate over the telephone, and read printed and digital material.
  • This role may require working outside standard business hours at times to address time-sensitive case situations or program needs.

Travel:

Minimal travel required. Occasional travel (estimated less than 15%) may be required for national leadership meetings, regional business reviews, or planning sessions.

title: Accessioning Team Runner
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:  On site position in Austin, TX

The Accessioning Team Runner collects, sorts, and transports packages to Accessioning laboratory in the Austin, TX office.  Hourly rate is $17.

 

Shift Options:
Monday-Friday, 9am-530pm
Hourly rate starts at $17

 

 PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Sort and transport packages from the Shipping dock to the Accessioning laboratory.

  • Pick up packages from the receptionist’s desk.

  • Scan all tracking numbers into a Google spreadsheet and ensure that tracking numbers are scanned in correctly and spreadsheet is filled out completely.

  • Distribute packages to the Clinical Data Operators (CDO) in a timely and efficient manner following distribution guidelines.

  • Rack samples that arrive in bulk (without individual kit boxes) ensuring that the paperwork matches up with the samples.

  • Escalate any issues or discrepancies to the Leads or Supervisor.

  • Empty bins filled with kit boxes at the CDO workstations into carts placed at designated locations in the lab.

  • Perform a visual check of the kit boxes to make sure that there is no PHI on the kit boxes or samples remaining in the discarded kit boxes.

  • Empty biohazard cans in the lab.

  • Scan bench worksheets.

  • Scan documents into cases.

  • Maintain tidiness of Runner workstations.

  • Store requisition forms by date into the filing cabinets.

  • Dispose of requisition forms into the shred bins that have exceeded the retention period.

  • Performs other duties as assigned.

  • Notify Supervisor and Leads of any packaging issues or discrepancies

  • This role works with PHI on a regular basis both in paper and electronic form and has access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic) in order to perform the job

  • Employee must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30 days of hire.

  • Must maintain a current status on Natera training requirements.

 

  • QUALIFICATIONS

  • High School Diploma (or equivalent) required.

  • Previous computer experience.

 

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Familiar with Google documents.

  • Ability to perform basic calculations.

  • Organized and self- motivated.

  • Ability to work quickly and efficiently.

 

 

 

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program!

For more information, visit www.natera.com.

Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide.

All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable laws.

If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents. 

Link: https://www.natera.com/notice-of-data-collection-california-residents/

Please be advised that Natera will reach out to candidates with a @natera.com email domain ONLY. Email communications from all other domain names are not from Natera or its employees and are fraudulent. Natera does not request interviews via text messages and does not ask for personal information until a candidate has engaged with the company and has spoken to a recruiter and the hiring team. Natera takes cyber crimes seriously, and will collaborate with law enforcement authorities to prosecute any related cyber crimes.

title: EH&S Lead
description:
About Arc Institute

Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.

Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:

  • Virtual Cell Initiative: Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets,  accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.
  • Alzheimer's Disease Initiative: Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.

More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.

About the position

As EH&S Lead, you will own the development, implementation, and the management of Arc’s Environmental, Health, and Safety programs and culture. You will design solutions that satisfy overlapping local, state, and federal requirements, and serve as Arc’s primary point of contact for regulatory and certifying agencies.

Your remit covers chemical hygiene, biosafety, OSHA compliance, medical and hazardous waste, and Arc’s safety permits and sustainability programs. You will hire and manage a biosafety manager and direct the work of outside vendors and consultants.

About you

  • You are deeply committed to the health and safety of your colleagues, and you achieve it through partnership with the labs rather than around them.
  • You are genuinely curious about the science here and want to understand the research at a real level of depth.
  • You thrive in a diverse environment and enjoy working with scientists and students from many backgrounds.
  • You are energized by building programs and forging cross-functional partnerships that strengthen the community and the mission.

In this position you will

  • Provide safety leadership and EH&S subject matter expertise aligned with Arc’s operating principles.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain EH&S programs, procedures, and systems in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, driving continuous improvement.
  • Develop Arc’s safety strategy and carry out safety policies and procedures in accordance with all applicable regulatory and organizational requirements.
  • Hire, manage, and develop a biosafety manager, setting clear priorities and standards for their work.
  • Advise Arc’s administrative team on safety and compliance for specific projects and operations.
  • Define Arc’s approach to  EH&S employee safety and onboarding training, with a focus on efficiency and engagement.
  • Own and evolve Arc’s compliance programs including, but not limited to, the Cal/OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard and biosafety program, chemical safety, radiation safety, and controlled substances.
  • Own Arc’s environmental compliance strategy, including the industrial wastewater discharge permit, hazardous waste requirements, and regulatory permitting.
  • Own risk assessment program and conduct regular risk assessments and safety audits to identify workplace hazards — chemical, physical, biological, industrial, and radiological among them — and remediate hazards or recommend improvements to reduce them.
  • Lead investigations of accidents, incidents, injuries, and complaints concerning potential hazards or unsafe conditions to determine root causes and preventive measures.
  • Conduct safety inspections and walkthroughs that deliver meaningful insight and surface continuous improvement opportunities across Arc’s labs.
  • Develop and manage EH&S management systems covering chemical inventories, SDS, near-miss reporting, permitting compliance, and incident investigations.
  • Oversee regulated medical and hazardous waste programs, including vendor contracting.
  • Act as primary point of contact for regulatory and certifying agencies and government authorities.

title: Building Engineer
description:
About Arc Institute

Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.

Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:

  • Virtual Cell Initiative: Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets,  accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.
  • Alzheimer's Disease Initiative: Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.

More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.

About the position

Arc Institute operates advanced wet-lab and research facilities where uptime directly protects irreplaceable science: cell lines, samples, and instruments representing years of work. We're hiring a hands-on Facilities Building Engineer to own the reliability of our building systems and lab-critical environments. 

This is a working engineer role. You will diagnose and fix problems yourself, and you’ll know when a job calls for a specialist. You will direct our vendor and contract-support partners to get it done right, on time, and on budget. You'll also run facility projects end-to-end and serve as the calm, service-oriented point of contact for the researchers who depend on the building.

About you

  • You catch problems early, before they turn into a researcher’s bad day. You’re just as comfortable running a diagnostic yourself as you are getting a vendor on the phone to handle something that’s not yours to touch. You want to know why a system works the way it does, not just how to patch it.
  • You like being around science, even though you’re not a scientist. You get that a freezer failure here isn’t an inconvenience; it’s years of someone’s work. That weight doesn’t stress you out. It’s part of what makes the job worth doing well.
  • You don’t need a lot of ramp-up time or close supervision to take ownership. You’re comfortable being the primary engineer onsite, you set your own priorities, and you integrate with the team from day one.
  • You’re straightforward and easy to track down. You build trust through consistent follow-through.

  • Serve as the primary onsite contact for facilities service requests; deliver responsive, professional service to researchers and staff.

  • Interpret and adjust the building automation system (e.g., Alerton, Automated Logic, Johnson Controls, Siemens)

  • Support compliance with Bay Area Air Quality Management District (BAAQMD) permits for generators and boilers, and with CUPA, hazardous materials, and wastewater-discharge requirements
  • Align building operations with CDC/NIH BMBL biosafety guidance in coordination with EH&S.
  • Drive energy efficiency and monitoring across high-load systems (compute/cooling, freezer farm), identifying sustainability and cost-reduction opportunities.

title: Literacy Coach
description:
About the Team

Michigan Online School (MOS) is a K-12 tuition-free online public school in the state of Michigan. At MOS, we empower students to be their best by enabling them to learn in ways that are right for them – using innovative technology at home, at their proper level, and at their own pace.

The Literacy Coach partners with teachers, school leaders, and instructional teams to strengthen literacy instruction and improve student achievement. Through job-embedded coaching, professional learning, collaborative planning, classroom modeling, and data-informed support, the Literacy Coach helps educators implement evidence-based literacy practices aligned with Michigan academic standards and state literacy initiatives.

The Literacy Coach works collaboratively with teachers, principals, leadership teams, and data specialists to build instructional capacity, support effective literacy interventions, strengthen reading outcomes, and promote continuous school improvement. This position emphasizes a collaborative, relationship-driven approach to professional growth and instructional excellence.

Eligibility: Open to residents of Michigan

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Instructional Coaching & Teacher Support

  • Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with teaching staff grounded in mutual respect, teamwork, and accountability.

  • Partner with classroom teachers to implement evidence-based early literacy instructional practices through job-embedded coaching.

  • Provide individualized and small-group coaching through classroom observations, instructional modeling, co-teaching, collaborative planning, goal-setting, and reflective conversations.

  • Model effective whole-group and small-group literacy instruction for teachers and students.

  • Support teachers in developing effective classroom literacy environments and implementing research-based instructional strategies and literacy programs.

  • Coach teachers in structured literacy lesson design and the implementation of practices aligned with state standards.

  • Provide ongoing feedback to help teachers reflect on, establish goals, practice, and refine instructional skills aligned with the Essential Instructional Practices in Literacy.

Data Analysis & Student Achievement

  • Analyze formative assessment, screening, and diagnostic data to develop and inform instructional plans.

  • Support teachers in collecting, analyzing, and using student data to guide instructional decisions and improve learning outcomes.

  • Administer and interpret universal screeners to identify students with characteristics of dyslexia.

title: Clinical Laboratory Scientist II
description:
Location: On-Site in Boulder, CO (Foresight Dx business unit, a Natera company)

Shift: Tuesday - Saturday, 11:30am-8:00pm

About our Company:

Foresight Diagnostics is a molecular diagnostics company pioneering non-invasive cancer detection through highly sensitive, cell-free DNA-based liquid biopsy technologies. Our proprietary methods - originally developed at Stanford University - are designed to detect smaller tumors earlier and enable more personalized treatment strategies for patients with cancer. 

We sit at the intersection of molecular biology, bioinformatics, and next-generation sequencing (NGS), and we translate rigorous science into clinically meaningful solutions. Following our acquisition by Natera, we now combine the agility of a mission-driven startup with the scale and resources of a global leader in cell-free DNA testing. It’s an exciting moment to join us. 

Headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, our team operates in a high accountability, collaborative environment where quality and continuous improvement aren’t just values - they’re how we work every day.

About the Role

The Clinical Laboratory Scientist II will be responsible for performing a variety of laboratory procedures involved in end-to-end processing of biological samples to enable successful downstream next-generation sequencing (NGS). Processing will include accessioning and both manual and automated extraction, library preparation, hybrid capture, sequencing and QC steps. Under the guidance of the Director of Clinical Laboratory Operations and the Laboratory Director, you will work collaboratively within the clinical laboratory leveraging your technical knowledge, skills and abilities to ensure efficient and quality results are provided to our clients and patients while also informing/participating in process improvements. This position will report to the Lab Manager.

 

What You Will Bring

  • Bachelor’s or Master's degree in chemical, physical, biological, or clinical laboratory science or medical technology from an accredited institution

    • Education received at a college or university located outside of the United States or United States Territories requires a credentials equivalency evaluation by an approved agency

  • Hold a current and active American Society of Clinical Pathology (ASCP) board certification

  • Hold current and valid Clinical Laboratory Scientist licensure (Generalist or CGMBS)

  • Demonstrate a working knowledge of the general biological principles that govern DNA biology

  • Possess a strong foundational understanding of common molecular biology techniques, such as PCR/qPCR, DNA ligation, and DNA extraction

  • Working level knowledge or ability to learn use of common molecular biology instruments; Agilent Tapestation/capillary electrophoresis, Qubit, plate readers, thermocyclers and other common laboratory instruments

  • Previous experience handling human biological materials is required

  • Working knowledge of how to safely operate in a BSL-2 environment is required

  • Previous experience handling, processing, and extracting DNA from biological specimens is required

 

What You Will Do

Technical

  • Perform routine and complex diagnostic laboratory testing on patient samples for clinical, biopharma, and academic partnerships.

  • Provide technical guidance and oversight to non-licensed personnel for pre-analytical, analytical and post-analytical activities.

  • Interpret data and results of all analyses according to set procedures and guidelines.

  • Support day to day operations by assisting with data entry, receiving samples and consumables, reagent preparation, sample preparation, temperature recording, laboratory maintenance and documentation.

  • Identify and resolve problems that may adversely affect test performance or reporting of test results following the escalation path to clinical leadership as needed.

  • Assist with research, translational research, regulated products through the execution of partnership studies and internal/external validation studies.

  • Participate as a contributing member of the clinical laboratory by assisting in routine activities, to include but not limited to general upkeep and stocking, SOP author and review, and continuous improvement.

  • Proposes assay and process improvements and conducts improvement activities under guidance.

  • Demonstrate forward thinking and initiative in work planning and execution of work in order to achieve on-time report delivery.

  • Participate in new or revised assay launches giving input on launch logistics as appropriate.

  • Participate in work planning initiatives and scheduling.

Quality, Training & Equipment

  • Maintaining documentation in compliance with Good Laboratory Practices and Quality Systems.

  • Assist with quality control and quality assurance activities. Responsible for reviewing and analyzing the health of laboratory quality metrics in collaboration with clinical leadership.

  • Complete initial training and maintain competencies as current and up to date for all trained assays.

  • Wear appropriate PPE as required and comply with safety rules and regulations.

  • Follow standard operating procedures (SOP).

  • Participate in IQ/OQ/PQ for equipment to ensure ability to train team members on proper use and maintenance as appropriate.

  • Escalate equipment issues that impact TAT or patient safety.

  • Assist, perform, and review instrument correlation studies. Collaborate with operational leadership on equipment analysis for assay expansion or improvement.

  • Perform instrument and procedural calibrations and maintenance.

  • Advises and drives progress on troubleshooting equipment issues.

  • Adhere to the laboratory's quality control policies including document control activities, change management, corrective preventative action.

  • May act as trainer in place of designated trainer/training team.

Team

  • Cultivate, build and maintain positive and collaborative relationships within teams and cross-functionally.

  • Operate as a thought leader and hold cross-functional teams accountable to regulatory, quality, scientific and performance standards to ensure the highest quality for sample integrity.

  • Seen as a role model for safety behavior standards and cultural tenets.

  • Serves as a leader from the bench, demonstrating consistency in good lab practices.

 

Working Conditions and Physical Effort

title: Scientist II, Screening
description:
Profluent is the frontier AI lab for biology. Profluent builds powerful foundation models for all of life's molecules, unlocking solutions that transform medicine, agriculture, and beyond. Founded in 2022 and headquartered in Emeryville, CA, Profluent is backed by leading investors including Altimeter Capital, Bezos Expeditions, Spark Capital, Insight Partners, Air Street Capital, AIX Ventures, and Convergent Ventures and has raised over $150M to date.

The Role

Profluent is seeking a motivated, rigorous, and collaborative scientist to establish and lead a centralized gene editor screening function. High-quality experimental data is a core input to our protein design models, and this role will own the screening operations that produce it.

This role centers on building and running a screening core responsible for assay standardization, data quality, and team development. At first, you will support campaigns that generate training and evaluation data for our protein design models, and the scope may grow to cover more programs. You will design, run, and troubleshoot mammalian genome editing assays with NGS readouts in arrayed and pooled formats. You will set the technical standards that make our data reproducible and trustworthy. You will also build and mentor a team of Research Associates, and coordinate closely with Automation, Bioinformatics, Data Science, and Biology to keep the screening pipeline running smoothly from start to finish.

As a leader of the team, you will balance hands-on scientific execution with people management and process development. You will identify, prioritize, and drive infrastructure projects that improve throughput, consistency, and assay sensitivity. You will also work with leadership to shape the long-term scope of the core.

We welcome candidates from diverse backgrounds who share our commitment to revolutionizing biology, driving meaningful innovation, and making a lasting impact on global healthcare.

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the future of AI-driven protein design while collaborating with a dynamic, interdisciplinary team of experts in machine learning, protein engineering, cell biology, and gene editing.

 

Responsibilities

Team Leadership

  • Build and lead a team of 2–4 Research Associates, including hiring, training, performance management, and career development
  • Train and mentor staff on aseptic technique, assay execution, and documentation standards
  • Foster a supportive team culture that prioritizes growth, engagement, and well-being

Execution

  • Prioritize, schedule, and resource cross-functional experiments in coordination with Automation and Bioinformatics
  • Design, execute, troubleshoot, and analyze mammalian genome editing assays with NGS readouts in arrayed and pooled formats
  • Onboard new assays and extend existing assays to new enzyme classes
  • Maintain sample chain of custody from plate mapping through automation, sample preparation, and sequencing submission, partnering with Bioinformatics on data schema and capture
  • Communicate technical results clearly to both expert and non-expert audiences
  • Deliver QC'd, analysis-ready datasets with documented QC flags to ML

Process Development

  • Define and enforce technical standards, and write and maintain SOPs
  • Qualify new assays and define acceptance criteria based on reproducibility data
  • Maintain cell line quality and inventory for screening assays, in coordination with teams that manage cell banks
  • Characterize assay sensitivity, including the minimum detectable difference in activity at standard replicate counts
  • Identify, prioritize, and plan infrastructure projects that continually improve assays and processes
  • Coordinate process development across Automation, Bioinformatics, Data Science, and Biology
  • Evaluate the costs and benefits of centralizing high-throughput workflows in partnership with other teams
  • Work with leadership to assess and refine the scope of core functions

 

Qualifications

  • PhD in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Cell Biology, or a related field and 2+ years of relevant industry experience, or MS in a related field and 10+ years of relevant industry experience
  • Hands-on experience with bacterial and mammalian cell culture, genome editing, and NGS-based assays
  • Experience with high-throughput experimentation and analysis of large datasets
  • Experience with LIMS or ELN systems for sample and experiment tracking
  • Demonstrated ability to establish technical standards and drive consistent execution across operators


Preferences

  • Experience working in or building a core facility or centralized service function
  • Track record of building or improving high-throughput processes
  • Experience leading infrastructure or process improvement projects
  • Experience with liquid handling automation and tech transfer
  • Experience with cell bank and inventory management
  • Strong foundation in experimental design and statistics, including power analysis and design of experiments (DOE)

title: Member of Technical Staff, Molecular & Cell Biologist
description:
About the team

We use evolution to structure, explore, and engineer biology. Our Deployment team applies Arcadia’s novel, validated platform and instrument technologies to bench research. The primary focus of the team is to quickly execute on technical projects for commercial partners, develop well-designed experimental case studies for our platform and products, and develop autonomous AI/wetlab iteration circuits for critical predictions and technologies.

The role

We're hiring a scientist with deep hands-on expertise in molecular and cell biology. As part of the Deployment team at Arcadia, you'll help us build our experimental assets and operating principles. You will take our most critical, unique approaches and make them robust and scalable. You'll work side-by-side with software and instrument engineers. The data you generate will, in many cases, inform models directly as we build towards several agentic lab-in-the-loop workflows that leverage Arcadia’s novel platform capabilities.

Levels

  • Scientist: PhD or PhD-level experience, plus at least 2 years full-time experience in industry. Should be capable of owning the experimental design and execution for projects.

description:
LOCATION: On-Site in Boulder, CO (Foresight Dx business unit, a Natera company)

 

ABOUT OUR COMPANY:

Foresight Diagnostics is a molecular diagnostics company pioneering non-invasive cancer detection through highly sensitive, cell-free DNA-based liquid biopsy technologies. Our proprietary methods - originally developed at Stanford University - are designed to detect smaller tumors earlier and enable more personalized treatment strategies for patients with cancer. 

We sit at the intersection of molecular biology, bioinformatics, and next-generation sequencing (NGS), and we translate rigorous science into clinically meaningful solutions. Following our acquisition by Natera, we now combine the agility of a mission-driven startup with the scale and resources of a global leader in cell-free DNA testing. It’s an exciting moment to join us. 

Headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, our team operates in a high accountability, collaborative environment where quality and continuous improvement aren’t just values - they’re how we work every day.

 

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Every liquid biopsy result starts at the bench, and this role puts you right there. As part of our Boulder R&D team, you’ll work hands-on with scientists developing ultrasensitive, cell-free DNA technology designed to detect smaller tumors earlier and enable more personalized treatment for patients with cancer. You’ll run experiments across the NGS workflow, from gDNA isolation and library prep to hybrid capture and sequencing, using automated liquid handlers and instruments like the TapeStation and Qubit. Along the way, you’ll learn to troubleshoot, keep instruments running smoothly, and understand why an experiment behaves the way it does, not just how to run it.

You won’t work in a silo. You’ll partner daily with Associates and Scientists, summarize and present your data to the team, and write SOPs that shape how we work. Your notebooks, results, and attention to detail will be trusted and relied on by the people around you. Foresight’s Stanford-born science now has the backing of Natera, a global leader in cell-free DNA testing, so you’ll get the agility of a mission-driven startup with the resources and reach of an established company. If you have a few years of molecular biology experience and want to build deep expertise in one of the most exciting areas of modern diagnostics, in a collaborative, high-accountability culture where quality and continuous improvement are part of everyday work, we’d love to meet you.

 

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

You will work primarily with R&D assisting Associates/Scientists in various lab duties. Responsibilities will include:

  • Independently execute simple experiments and perform basic troubleshooting 
  • Produce competent, reproducible results to a high technical standard
  • Maintain accurate and well-organized laboratory records, worksheets and notebooks
  • Summarize data in spreadsheets, graphs and presentations
  • Write standard operating procedures (SOP) and other lab-related documents as needed
  • Maintain equipment and instruments in good operating condition, recognize any malfunctions and troubleshoot as needed
  • Utilize molecular biology techniques in performing laboratory tests. This role will have occasional access to PHI both in paper and electronic form and have occasional access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic) in order to perform the job.
  • Adhere to environmental, health and safety (EHS) guidelines and good laboratory practices (GLP)
  • Perform other tasks as specified by the manager/director

 

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • BS/BA in a biological science or equivalent
  • Minimum of 2 years Molecular Biology laboratory experience required

 

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

  • gDNA isolation from biological samples (preferred).
  • Experience with library preparation for next generation sequencing and sequencing platforms 
  • Experience with hybrid capture technologies
  • Experience with laboratory automated liquid handler platforms
  • Sample analysis/QC on the Agilent Tapestation, Nanodrop, Qubit, electrophoresis
  • Must have proven interpersonal, communication, computer, and technical skills.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills required.
  • Microsoft Excel experience required

Compensation & Total Rewards 

This range reflects a good-faith estimate of the base pay we reasonably expect to offer at the time of hire. Final compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and internal equity considerations.

  • Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Generous paid time off and company holidays
  • Additional wellness and work-life benefits

Compensation Range 

$74,800.00 - $89,000.00

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. The Manufacturing Lead will be responsible for the manufacturing and analysis of a variety of gene products across Twist Bioscience’s proprietary process workflow to meet the Twist production forecast and timelines. The Manufacturing Lead will be held accountable for maintaining production schedule and troubleshooting, guiding the work of other shift associates while also performing manufacturing tasks. What You’ll Be Doing 

  • Assisting the production supervisor and guiding the work performed on the manufacturing floor by manufacturing associates. 
  • Troubleshooting all processes related to manufacturing process and instrumentation.
  • Taking responsibility for daily operations when the supervisor is not available.
  • Maintaining daily operations w/ or w/o the supervisor (equipment maintenance, fulfill production request, retain review)

  • Overseeing material inventory and waste management activities for the shift.
  • Monitoring the flow of intermediate products through the Manufacturing Execution System (MES) and notifying the supervisor of any discrepancies.

  • Training new laboratory manufacturing associates.

  • Operating laboratory equipment and liquid handling robots (Hamilton Stars, centrifuges, sealers, thermocyclers, spectrometers, Illumina Next-Gen sequencers etc.) 
  • Effectively using molecular and cell biology processes and techniques, especially PCR, DNA quantitation,  purification and cloning.
  • Maintain thorough, accurate and detailed documentation of all work performed using existing document templates and applications.
  • Updating and writing work instructions and documentation.
  • Working independently and in a safe manner.
  • Paying great attention to detail and yielding consistent results.
  • Performing troubleshooting and handling process deviations correctly.
  • Analyzing data outcomes from manufacturing steps and deciding on or recommending a course of action.
  • Following lean manufacturing, ISO and GMP practices.

  • Must be able to stand for long periods of time while performing duties

  • Must be able to lift up to 20 lbs

description:
About the team

We use evolution to structure, explore, and engineer biology. Our Deployment team applies Arcadia’s novel, validated platform and instrument technologies to bench research. The primary focus of the team is to quickly execute on technical projects for commercial partners, develop well-designed experimental case studies for our platform and products, and develop autonomous AI/wetlab iteration circuits for critical predictions and technologies.

The role

We're hiring a scientist with deep hands-on expertise in biochemistry. As part of the Deployment team at Arcadia, you'll help us build our experimental assets and operating principles. You will take our most critical, unique approaches and make them robust and scalable. You'll work side-by-side with software and instrument engineers. The data you generate will, in many cases, inform models directly as we build towards several agentic lab-in-the-loop workflows that leverage Arcadia’s novel platform capabilities.

Levels

  • Scientist: PhD or PhD-level experience, plus at least 2 years full-time experience in industry. Should be capable of owning the experimental design and execution for projects.

Requirements

Technical

  • Hands-on recombinant protein expression and purification
  • Familiarity with protein quality control and biophysical characterization, such as SDS-PAGE, thermal stability, and aggregation measurements
  • Experience developing and running quantitative activity or binding assays, such as enzyme kinetics, BLI, SPR, or fluorescence-based binding assays
  • Experience developing and running quantitative stability assays, such as DLS and SLS
  • Comfort fitting kinetic and binding data to appropriate models and confidence interpreting the reliability and utility of these results

General

  • Demonstrated ability to anticipate and test new use cases and considerations for scientific tools and assays

title: Scientist I, Synthetic Biology
description:
The Role: 

Generate’s Prototyping Lab builds the experimental systems that let us measure protein function at unprecedented scale. By combining synthetic biology, large DNA libraries, high-throughput assays, and machine learning, the team creates workflows that turn complex biological questions into rich, usable datasets. 

We’re looking for two Scientists with a strong record in experimental synthetic biology to develop pooled screens capable of testing hundreds of thousands of protein variants in parallel to identify protein binders and modulators. You’ll shape these experiments via DNA library design, pooled in vitro protein display, and NGS-based enrichment analysis. For one of the two roles, we are looking for a Scientist who additionally has experience in mammalian cell engineering and membrane protein studies. Experience in computational modeling or statistical analysis would help you connect experimental design to the quality and usefulness of the resulting data. 

You’ll work closely with Protein Sciences and Machine Learning teams to build screening approaches that deliver clear, quantitative insight into protein function. The role offers substantial scope to originate and advance new technologies, with close collaboration across a well-resourced biotech team.

Here's how you will contribute:

  • Build pooled screening workflows to achieve scalable protein binding and functional readouts, from assay setup through data interpretation.
  • Collaboratively establish reliable assay conditions, quantitative measures, and handoff plans that enable project teams to maximize platform utility.
  • Identify opportunities to test unconventional hypotheses, applying the strongest concepts for drug program acceleration and supporting IP filings.  
  • Synthesize findings into clear recommendations, and present them in presentations and in writing to colleagues across disciplines.
  • Use quantitative reasoning, modeling, and critical literature review to inform experimental choices. 

The Ideal Candidate will have:

  • PhD in synthetic or systems biology, bioengineering or a related field with 0-1 year of experience; alternatively, a bachelor’s or master’s degree with at least 6 years of highly relevant experience.
  • Hands-on experience designing and running pooled binding screens, ideally using both purified proteins and cell-based assays.
  • For one of the roles, we are seeking strong cell-culture skills, including experience engineering cell lines for screening applications using methods such as CRISPR, lentiviral transduction, or transposon-based integration; experience working with membrane proteins is also highly preferred.  
  • Experience designing and building pooled DNA libraries, and using next-generation sequencing to track enrichment in selection campaigns.
  • Familiarity with recombinant protein production, purification, and/or binding assays is an advantage.
  • Ability to interpret complex screening data and write scripts in Python or a similar language; familiarity with AI-assisted coding tools such as Cursor or other LLM-based platforms.
  • Applies quantitative reasoning and sound experimental judgment to assess data quality, troubleshoot assays, and guide next steps.
  • Takes ownership of applied biology projects from initial concept through execution, analysis, and delivery.
  • Brings intellectual curiosity to new technical challenges, shares expertise readily, and helps colleagues grow through collaboration and mentorship.
  • High level of cross-functional autonomy and self-motivation. 

Who will love this job: 

  • Biologists who integrate computational insight with experimentation to tackle complex problems.
  • Experimentalists who enjoy making difficult targets, including membrane proteins, tractable for pooled binding screens.
  • Platform builders who value assay robustness, data quality, and interpretable results alongside throughput. 

#LI-HM1

About Generate Biomedicines

We are a clinical-stage generative biology company pioneering the AI revolution in drug design and development. We are advancing a new approach to drug creation—one grounded in the ability to design proteins with defined biological intent. By integrating machine learning with large-scale experimentation, this approach aims to reduce the uncertainty, time, and cost associated with developing protein-based medicines.

Founded in 2018, we are advancing a growing pipeline of clinical and preclinical programs across multiple disease areas and protein modalities. By unifying computational design and clinical development within a single operating model, we translate this approach into clinical-stage programs and are leading a shift from traditional drug discovery toward systematic drug generation.

At Generate:Biomedicines, we collaborate across disciplines in new ways to invent and innovate. We bring diverse perspectives to a shared goal of delivering better medicines to patients in need, faster, guided by our values and leadership behaviors.

title: Product Manager, Platform
description: We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era. When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done. Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma. We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today. ROLE OVERVIEW AI is only as good as the data underneath it. Schemas is the configuration layer where customers model their scientific data and processes. It's the customer-defined data model that makes Benchling different from a point solution, and the contract every other system (internal apps, integrations, AI agents) relies on when reading or writing to Benchling. Get it right, and AI inherits a solid foundation; get it wrong, every layer above inherits the problem. As Schemas PM, you own the primitives (schema types, computed fields, fieldsets, constraints, static properties, data versioning) that every other team at Benchling builds on top of. This is one of the highest-leverage, most technically interesting roles on the platform team, and one we're investing in now as AI features across Benchling increasingly depend on the quality of the underlying data model. RESPONSIBILITIES Set product direction for Schemas and ship toward it incrementally, balancing fast prototyping with the platform stability admins and developers depend on. Relentlessly track how customers use Schemas — where it delights, where it fails — and build sharp personas and job-to-be-done context for each user type (admins, scientists, computational teams, internal and external developers). Bring customer "why," not just feature requests, back to Engineering and Design; partner with them closely to ship new capabilities. Champion structured, well-modeled data as the foundation for AI value across Benchling, anticipating what schema consumers will need next. Partner with Customer Experience, Field, Sales, and Marketing to get customer signal into the roadmap early. Partner closely with other Platform and Apps PMs — schemas underpin nearly every other platform surface, so alignment on sequencing and shared abstractions matters as much as your own roadmap. QUALIFICATIONS Energized by platform work and systems thinking; comfortable building the right abstraction ahead of need. Has designed, owned, or significantly evolved a data-modeling, schema, or configuration system used by external developers or technical admins — not just consumed one as a feature. Becomes the go-to person for customers, field, and engineers — not a router to engineering. Deep, demonstrated discovery practice: has built personas and JTBD frameworks from scratch, not just used ones handed to them. Track record balancing long-term vision with incremental shipping. Strong communicator across technical and executive audiences; B2B SaaS or developer-platform background preferred. Genuine curiosity about the science behind the data. You don't need a science background, but you should want one by the end of your first quarter here. HOW WE WORK Flexible Hybrid Work: We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. #LI-EK1 Benchling welcomes everyone. We also consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law, including but not limited to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

title: Medical Lab Scientist I
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:


Natera is currently seeking a licensed Medical Laboratory Scientist to analyze specimens and maintains equipment in good operating condition.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:


• Verify the proper specimen being analyzed and perform tests that need to be completed
• Proficient at analyzing clinical laboratory specimens following the standard methods and procedures in an efficient manner with little to no errors
• Responsible for maintaining updated understanding and knowledge of methods performed in the lab
• Provides general oversight of personnel and the daily operations in the lab.
• Meet expected performance metrics within role as applicable.
• Follows GLP (good laboratory practice): maintain clean and organized workspace
• Completes training and other deadlines on time.
• Provide guidance for new Clinical Laboratory Operator and/or Medical Laboratory Scientists.
• Train on specialized instructions for instruments/protocols (super users)
• Recognizes and escalates equipment malfunctions; troubleshoots common analytical and processing errors according to the laboratory’s standard operating procedure
• Recognizes, documents, and escalates protocol deviations in lab to lead/supervisor
• Assists with documentation for nonconformance reports.
• Participates in the updating of departmental standard operating procedures and database to accurately reflect the current practices.
• Conducts independent continuous improvement projects
• Ensures compliance with all regulatory agency requirements through proper documentation (example maintenance logs, bench worksheet)
• Performs quality control procedures to ensure accuracy of clinical data (if applicable)
• Maintains equipment and instruments in good operating condition (such as calibration and expiration date)
• Maintain inventory of material, supplies and equipment in the laboratory for performance of duties.
• Communicates with team and other departments on various platforms (including via e-mail)
• Provides feedback on day-to-day schedule and tasks to lead/supervisor; offers suggestions/ideas for improvement
• Assists teammates in completing daily tasks and facilitate workflow as needed
• Conducts himself/herself in a professional manner; acts as a role model/mentor to others
• Adheres to Departmental Expectations
• This role works with PHI on a regular basis both in paper and electronic form and have access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic) in order to perform the job
• Employee must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30 days of hire.
• Must maintain a current status on Natera training requirements.
• Performs other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • BS/BA degree in Medical Technology, Biological Sciences, or a related field
  • Current MT/MLS/CLS/MB certification preferable from ASCP, AMT, or AAB 


KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:


• Excellent interpersonal, communication, computer, troubleshooting, and pipetting skills.
• Experience in Molecular Biology preferred.
• Excellent oral and written communication skills.
• Word processing and data management skills.
• Ability to work well in a group
• Ability to work independently, with minimal supervision

 

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT:


• Duties typically performed in BSL-1 to 2 laboratories with potentially hazardous material
• Standing or sitting for long periods of time may be necessary
• Duties may require working weekends and overtime
• Must be able to lift boxes or supplies up to 35lbs
• Duties require wearing safety goggles, gloves, and laboratory coat.
• Duties require exposure to cold air due to frequent accessing of refrigeration and/or freezer units.

 

Must be able to discern color visually [or be able to evaluate cellular morphology when applicable] and pass applicable screening assessment

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. title: Analytics Engineer
description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centered creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Role Overview

The Analytics Engineer role serves as a key member of the Measurement Enablement team, responsible for ensuring client healthcare marketing data is accurate, current, and ready for reporting and analysis. This role bridges the gap between Data Engineering, analytics teams, and client stakeholders by managing data ingestion processes, validating data quality, maintaining reporting-ready data structures, and resolving issues throughout the data lifecycle. 

The ideal candidate enjoys investigating data questions, identifying root causes of data discrepancies, improving data quality, and working across multiple teams to ensure reliable data powers business decisions. 

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—New York City, Boston, Chicago, San Francisco, Indianapolis, or Lambertville (NJ)—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs.

Primary Responsibilities 

Data Ingestion & Source Management 

  • Coordinate the onboarding of new client data sources and data feeds.  
  • Partner with Data Engineering to ensure successful ingestion of data into Databricks.  
  • Monitor data delivery schedules and ingestion processes.  
  • Maintain source documentation, field mappings, and data inventories.  
  • Work directly with internal teams and external partners to resolve source-related issues. 

Data Quality & Stewardship 

  • Monitor data freshness, completeness, and accuracy across client datasets.  
  • Perform ongoing quality assurance and reconciliation checks.  
  • Investigate missing, unexpected, or inconsistent data.  
  • Escalate, coordinate and resolve remediation efforts with the appropriate teams.  
  • Maintain documentation of data quality findings and resolutions.  
  • Support the development of automated data quality checks and monitoring processes. 

Data Modeling 

  • Develop and maintain client-specific standard, custom, and master tables and reporting views within Databricks based on a medallion architecture.  
  • Assist with transforming and standardizing data from multiple sources into reporting-ready structures. 
  • Solve problems and help build solutions related to the data model to meet evolving reporting and analysis needs. 
  • Document business rules, transformation logic, and metric definitions.  
  • Support maintenance of reusable reporting datasets and standardized data models. 

Stakeholder Support 

  • Act as the primary point of contact for routine data-related questions.  
  • Partner with Client Services, Media, Strategy, and Data teams to align on data outputs and expectations. 
  • Work with analysts and measurement leads to understand reporting requirements, translate into technical requirements, and provide database-modeled data for reporting.  
  • Communicate data issues, impacts, and resolutions to stakeholders.  
  • Assist with troubleshooting data discrepancies impacting reporting deliverables. 

Reporting Support 

  • Support Power BI developers and business analysts with data-related questions.  
  • Assist with report validation and troubleshooting.  
  • Help verify data displayed in dashboards aligns with source systems and business requirements.  
  • Provide support for semantic models and reporting datasets when needed. 

Qualifications

  • Strong SQL and Python skills, in a Databricks environment preferrable. 
  • Experience using ETL tools and data manipulation concepts (Funnel.io, DBT, or similar applications). 
  • Comfort partnering with Data Engineering on data sources, schemas, and refresh logic. 
  • Deep analytical and problem-solving skills related to data storage and structure for reporting.
  • Experience reviewing data logic, KPI definitions, and QA outputs. 
  • Basic BI (Tableau, Power BI) skills including data modeling, dashboard structure, calculated fields, usability, data storytelling. 
  • Strong written and verbal communication with technical and non-technical stakeholders. 
  • Ability to translate complex business reporting requests into modeled data to support current and future analysis. 

Preferred / Bonus 

  • Pharma, HCP, or healthcare media analytics experience, including experience with media PLD (Physician Level Data).  
  • Digital media measurement expertise (media KPIs, attribution concepts, omnichannel analysis). 
  • Experience inheriting or stabilizing existing data warehouse schemas. 

Pay Range: $90,000-$110,000

The Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time.

title: アカウントエグゼクティブ・シニアアカウントエグゼクティブ
description:
Avalere Healthについて
私たちは、「すべての患者さんに可能性を届ける」という共通の目的のもとで働いています。Avalere Healthは、すべての患者さんが必要な治療、支援、ケアを等しく受けられることを目指しています。Advisory、Medical、Marketingの各チームがそれぞれの専門性を生かして連携し、ヘルスケアが障壁とならず、誰一人取り残されない未来を築いています。
このミッションを実現するためには、社員一人ひとりが目的意識を持ち、患者さんの人生に具体的な変化を生み出せる環境が必要です。私たちは、多様なバックグラウンドやスキルを生かし、自分らしく働きながら、世界中の患者さんのために力を発揮できる文化づくりに取り組んでいます。
私たちは柔軟な働き方を大切にしています。各グローバルチームは、チームやクライアントのニーズに応じて、オフィス勤務または在宅勤務を選択できます。ロンドン、マンチェスター、ワシントンD.C.、ニューヨークの主要拠点に加え、世界各地のオフィスが、必要な時にチームが集まるコラボレーション拠点となっています。在宅勤務の社員にも、交流の機会や必要なリソースを提供しています。
インクルーシブな文化は、私たちのすべての活動の中心にあります。Diverse Ability、Family、Gender、LGBTQ+、Mental Health、Race/Ethnicityの6つのEmployee Network Groupを通じて、社員が自分らしく働ける環境を支援しています。これらのグループは、定期的なミーティングや活動を通じて、多様性、公平性、インクルージョンを促進し、つながり、学び、交流する機会を提供しています。また、私たちはFertility Friendly認定企業として、不妊治療に関する方針、充実した育児休暇制度、柔軟な働き方を通じて、家族形成のあらゆる段階にある社員を支援しています。
日々のキャリア経験、数千に及ぶオンデマンド研修、定期的なキャリア対話、グローバルかつ部門横断的なキャリア機会を通じて、社員の継続的な成長を積極的に支援しています。


ポジションについて
Avalere Healthのグローバルマーケティング部門で、クライアント案件の日々の進行を支えるアカウントエグゼクティブを募集します。クライアントパートナーシップ、プロジェクトマネジメント、クリエイティブ、ストラテジーなどのメンバーと連携し、案件が予定どおり、正確かつ円滑に進むよう調整するポジションです。
会議の準備や議事録、進捗・アクション管理、ブリーフ作成の支援、承認状況の確認など、案件運営の土台となる業務を担当します。細かな点まで丁寧に確認し、リスクや課題を早めに共有しながら、自分の担当業務を着実に前へ進めることが求められます。
入社後は、クライアント業務を通じて、アカウントマネジメントの基礎を実践的に身につけていただきます。周囲の支援を受けながら担当範囲を広げ、将来的にはクライアントとのやり取りや、より複雑な案件進行にも関わっていただくことを期待しています。
 福利厚生・働き方 Avalere Health Japanでは、柔軟な働き方と、社員一人ひとりが能力を発揮できる職場環境を大切にしています。 休暇・福利厚生制度については、日本法人の雇用条件および社内規程に基づいて提供します。 また、グローバルネットワークとの協働、継続的な学習機会、専門性を高めるためのサポートを通じて、社員の成長とキャリア開発を支援します。 応募者の皆さまへ Avalere Healthへ応募される前に、応募者向けプライバシー通知をご確認ください。 応募者向けプライバシー通知を開く
